title: Removing supers after the honey harvest
subtitle: Empty supers go back onto the hive to be cleaned by the bees, then off before the autumn feed. Timing matters.
excerpt: After extraction, the frames still hold residual honey in every cell. Returning them to the hive lets the bees clean them out, then the beekeeper removes the frames dry and stores them. Using a clearer board prevents you having to brush thousands of bees off every frame by hand. Here is the sequence and the timing.
sourceNotes: NBU Beekeeper's Toolkit (2024), end-of-season management section. BBKA Bee Craft, late summer management notes. Frank Pearson, Bee-keeping for All (1923), Internet Archive, chapter on taking the honey. British Beekeepers Association seasonal calendar guidance.

glossaryTerms.definition: A board with one-way bee escapes (usually Porter bee escapes or round escape inserts) that allows bees to move down from the supers into the brood box but not return. Placed under the supers for 24–48 hours to empty them.

A small spring-loaded bee escape that fits into a standard hole in a crown board or clearer board. Bees pass through in one direction; the springs prevent return. Named after the British manufacturer.

content.text: Extracted super frames returned to the hive are cleaned out by the bees in two or three days. The bees take the residual honey down to the brood box and leave the frames dry and white. Fit a
below the supers to clear the bees down before you collect the frames. Without one, every frame has hundreds of bees to move, most of them reluctant to leave.
Returning supers to the hive for cleaning
Return extracted supers to the hive on the day of extraction or the day after. The fresher the frames, the faster and more thoroughly the bees clean them.
Stack extracted supers above the queen excluder. The bees will move up through the excluder and clean without risk of the queen laying in the super frames.
Leave for 2-3 days until the frames look dry and white.
springs are clean and not blocked. A blocked escape means no bees clear overnight.
Fit the clearer board (with escape hole uppermost, so the bees exit downward into the brood area) between the super and the top of the hive body.
Leave for 24-48 hours. A hot day clears faster than a cool one. In a good summer week, 24 hours is usually enough.
Check the super is empty of bees before removing. Lift a corner of the super and look for bees still on the frames. If more than a dozen remain, leave another 12 hours.

Stack cleaned frames in supers and close them with crown boards top and bottom. Store in a cool, dry, dark space away from wax moth. The most reliable protection against wax moth in stored combs is moth traps inside the stack, or leaving the stack in a cold space (below 10°C) where wax moth larvae are dormant.

Do not leave super frames exposed or stacked outside. Robbing will begin immediately, foragers from other hives will find any residual honey and strip the frames, creating a robbing frenzy that disturbs your hive.
